title: Space Link Extension—Application Program Interface for the Forward Space Packet Service
short_title: SLE API for the FSP Service (CCSDS 916.3-M-2)
organisation: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS)
status_notes: The Document Control table (PDF p. 7) marks issue 2 (September 2015) as the current issue and 916.3-M-1 (October 2008) as superseded. Issue 2 updates the text for the current SLE service specification, differentiates applicability by service generation, and updates the references.
summary:
A CCSDS Magenta Book that adds the **Forward Space Packet (FSP)**-specific part of the SLE Application Program Interface. The generic C++ API (component model, service instances, operation objects, proxies) is defined in the API core specification [CCSDS 914.0-M-2](../library/ccsds-914-0-914x0m2c1.md). This book adds what an implementation needs to provide or use the [SLE FSP service](../ccsds/sle/fsp.md), which carries telecommand Space Packets to a ground station that runs [COP-1](../ccsds/cop-1.md) on its behalf. It is the FSP counterpart of the RAF API book [CCSDS 915.1-M-2](../library/ccsds-915-1-915x1m2.md). See also [SLE over TCP/IP and the SLE API](../ccsds/sle/isp1-and-api.md).

Section 1 states that two FSP generations are supported: Generation 2 (BIND version 1, FSP B-1) and Generation 3 (BIND version 4, FSP B-2). There is no Generation 1. Section 2 extends the API model with FSP SI User and FSP SI Provider classes. The provider exports three interfaces. IFSP_SIAdmin holds the configuration (APID list, MAP list, virtual channel, maximum frame and packet length, blocking and multiplexing settings, packet buffer size). IFSP_FOPMonitor holds the FOP-1 parameters (sliding window, timer, transmission limit, V(S), FOP state). IFSP_SIUpdate receives the production events (packet started, radiated or acknowledged, buffer empty, production status change, VC aborted, directive completed). Table 2-1 maps each event to the status parameters it updates and the FSP-ASYNC-NOTIFY it triggers. A long subsection explains which checks are left to the application in multi-threaded designs: production status, blocked state, time windows, and APID/version/type checks on the opaque packet data. It also explains the special return handling for TRANSFER-DATA, INVOKE-DIRECTIVE and THROW-EVENT. Section 3 gives the normative component behaviour and diagnostic ordering, and Annex A (about 90 pages) gives the C++ types, operation objects and service instance interfaces.

key_points.text: The book specifies only the FSP-specific extensions to the SLE API core: functionality, interfaces and externally visible behaviour. It does not cover implementations, internal design or communications technology.

Two FSP generations are supported: Generation 2 (BIND version 1, FSP 912.3-B-1) and Generation 3 (BIND version 4, FSP 912.3-B-2). Generation 1 does not apply because the first FSP issue was written as part of Generation 2. Generation 2 support is for backward compatibility for a limited time.

The FSP SI Provider exports IFSP_SIAdmin (configuration), IFSP_FOPMonitor (FOP parameters, used only to answer GET-PARAMETER) and IFSP_SIUpdate (production events). The application must keep the FOP parameters updated, whatever the service instance state.

IFSP_SIUpdate methods are PacketStarted, PacketRadiated, PacketAcknowledged, BufferEmpty, PacketNotStarted, ProductionStatusChange, VCAborted, NoDirectiveCapability, DirectiveCapabilityOnline, DirectiveCompleted and EventProcCompleted. Each updates status parameters and may trigger an FSP-ASYNC-NOTIFY.

Configuration parameters include apid-list, blocking-timeout-period, blocking-usage, directive-invocation-enabled, map-list, maximum-frame-length, maximum-packet-length, segment-header, VC multiplexing control and scheme, virtual-channel and maximum-packet-buffer-size. Generation 3 adds bit-lock-required and rf-available-required.
The FOP parameters handled are fop-sliding-window, timeout-type, timer-initial, transmission-limit, transmitter-frame-sequence-number, fop-state, and MAP multiplexing control and scheme.
Status counters are kept separately for AD (sequence-controlled) and BD (expedited) packets received, processed and radiated, plus number-of-packets-acknowledged and packet-buffer-available.
Production status 'halted' rejects both BIND and START. 'Interrupted' accepts BIND but rejects START. 'Configured' and 'operational' accept both.

Several TRANSFER-DATA invocations can be in transit. When a check fails, the service element may therefore pass the operation to the application, which inserts the next expected packet identification and buffer size. INVOKE-DIRECTIVE and THROW-EVENT are handled the same way.

When a packet cannot be processed (non-operational production or expired latest start time), the service instance becomes blocked until the user sends FSP-STOP and then FSP-START. A blocked AD mode is cleared by a TRANSFER-DATA with mode 'sequence controlled and unblock AD'.
The API treats packets as opaque, so the service element is not required to check APID, packet version or packet type. These checks are left to the application.

notes: PDF pages 1-2 are duplicate covers. The extracted text has 155 form-feed pages (registry: 154); the last one is empty. Table 2-1 is printed in landscape and comes out of the extraction with its footer and page labels interleaved with the cells. The class diagram (Figure 2-1) survives as an attribute list. Oddities as printed: the API core specification is reference [4] in the reference list, but 1.1, 2.1 and several clauses (for example 2.2.3.1.10 and 2.2.9.3) cite it as reference [5], which is the C++ standard. The Foreword says 'This Recommended Standard is therefore subject ...', and 1.6.2.1 speaks of 'this Recommended Standard', although the book is a Recommended Practice. 1.5.2 swaps Parts 2 and 3 of the cross support model, as in the RAF API book. The normative FSP reference is issue 2 (912.3-B-2, July 2010), one issue older than the library's FSP book (ccsds-912-3-912x3b3s, issue 3 of August 2016, historical copy). Companion library items are ccsds-914-0-914x0m2c1 (API core) and ccsds-915-1-915x1m2 (RAF API). No individual authors are named. The registry copy was taken from ccsds.org on 2026-11-12.
